articles.title: España, campeón por equipos, gana el último duelo ante Euskadi del Mundial
articles.standfirst: Se impuso en la final de pala corta por parejas
articles.summary: Se impuso en la final de pala corta por parejas
articles.body: España, que se consagró campeón por equipos en el Mundial de pelota vasca de Buenos Aires, ganó este sábado el último duelo ante Euskadi por el título masculino de pala corta por parejas. El partido debió resolverse en set de desempate. La Roja festejó la cima del medallero general del certamen, con siete medallas de oro, nueve de plata y dos de bronce. El equipo español se había asegurado el campeonato incluso antes de disputar tres de las cuatro finales jugadas este sábado tras los resultados de Argentina, México y Euskadi, que lo siguieron en ese orden en la clasificación definitiva. En la última jornada del Mundial, los españoles Javier Inchaustig y Carlos Baeza, sustituido por lesión en el segundo set por Emiliano Skufka, derrotaron a los vascos por 9-15, 15-11 y 10-5 en el tercer juego. Para Euskadi fue una jornada algo difícil, ya que también cayeron en la final pelota adaptada contra Francia, aunque esa competencia no sumó para el medallero. Argentina, apoyado por su ferviente público, se impuso a continuación en el mismo escenario en la final de paleta cuero masculina por 2-0 tras un vibrante partido en el que Román Maldonado y Mateo Billoron superaron a los ibéricos Baeza y Javier Labiano por 15-12 y 15-9. España también fue vencida en la final de frontball femenino ante México, que se quedó además con el oro de la rama masculina. El trinquete del club Ciudad de Buenos Aires alojó las últimas dos finales del Mundial. En paleta goma femenina, las argentinas Sabrina Andrade y Lucía Lumini remontó un partido que parecía difícil y se impuso por 13-15, 15-5 y 10-3. En la rama masculina de la misma disciplina, Argentina con Sebastián Andreassen y Guillermo Osorio venció en sets corridos a Oan Darribat y Kevin Pucheux, de Francia 15-3 y 15-6. Los tres últimos encuentros del sábado permitieron a Argentina arrebatar el segundo puesto del medallero general a México al superarlo en cantidad de oros. Así, España lideró el medallero de este Mundial con siete oros, nueve platas y dos bronces; Argentina con cinco oros y tres bronces; México con cuatro oros y seis bronces; Euskadi con tres oros, ocho platas y un bronce; Francia con dos oros, cinco platas y seis bronces; Estados Unidos con una plata y un bronce; Cuba con un bronce; y Uruguay con un bronce.

articles.title: Mark Allen suggests he could play in UK Championship as he continues treatment for mental health struggles
articles.summary: Mark Allen has indicated that the UK Championship is in his sights; the world No 12 says he is determined to shine a light on mental health issues; If you are affected by this story, please visit sky.com/viewersupport
articles.body:
The Northern Irishman, who won the tournament in 2022, cast doubt on continuing his career in an emotional interview following his recent Northern Ireland Open exit.

However Allen, who received an outpouring of support having revealed he is receiving treatment in a mental health clinic, has now suggested the competition is in his sights.

On Sunday morning, Allen wrote on social media: "Completely overwhelmed by all the messages I have received since my statement. As I continue my treatment and my recovery now I know that I simply have to raise more awareness around mental health in the future.

"Best part of six weeks before the UK Championships starts and all being well I'll be in a better place by then but for now it's just one day at a time.

"Thanks again for all your support. It's meant so so much to myself and my family."

After his Northern Ireland Open defeat to compatriot Jordan Brown, Allen told TNT Sports he "doesn't see a future with snooker in it" in an interview that sparked a considerable online support for the world No 12.

The Antrim native was playing his first match since his World Championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in April - when he missed a match-ball black off the spot at 16-15 in front and went on to lose a decider.

The 40-year-old has since stayed away from the tour due to personal issues that he has kept private, but are understood not to relate to any repercussions from the manner of his defeat at the Crucible.

Allen has been among the world's top players for a long time, winning both UK and Masters titles in a total of 12 ranking tournament wins, and has reached the world championship semi-finals three times.

A day after his NI Open loss, Allen released a statement via social media thanking everyone for their messages after his interview the previous day, and reassuring fans that his current mental state is the best it's been in months after receiving care.

"Everything I said in that interview was true," Allen wrote. "However, rest assured I'm doing my best to turn things around," he said.

"I have been in a mental health clinic for the last 10 weeks, finally discharging so I could attempt to play in Belfast.

"I owed that to my family, in particular my daughter to see me play for what could be the last time... I also owed it to the fans who have supported me throughout my 21 years on tour.

"I'm not okay, but I'm okay in that itself. I've been much worse in the last few months than you saw yesterday. I literally didn't see a future in anything.

"My daughter kept me going, the therapists, staff and all the other patients were amazing and helped me through some really dark days.

"I see the light now that I couldn't see before but I do now. I also know it won't happen overnight. I'm a work in progress.

"My fight and determination on the table has always been there for ones to see. I need to show those same fighting qualities off it now for a while."

articles.title: Pakistan drops Shan Masood from Sri Lanka Test squad as Agha, Rizwan return
articles.summary: Ali Usman has also been recalled to the Test team after being sent home from the England tour.
articles.body:
Former skipper Salman Agha has returned to Pakistan’s Test cricket squad for the upcoming series against Sri Lanka, but there was still no place for Mohammad Rizwan following the team’s disastrous tour of England.

Agha and Rizwan were among seven players expelled from the Test tour of England in August, a series the visitors lost 3-0 .

In Pakistan’s first squad since, five players remain out of favour, including wicketkeeper-batsman Rizwan, who is the subject of an ongoing investigation by the country’s cybercrime agency.

Earlier this week, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) allowed Rizwan to feature in a domestic match.

Agha was left out of this month’s T20 series against Sri Lanka, but the 32-year-old impressed in the ongoing One-Day International (ODI) series at home, scoring a century against Sri Lanka last Sunday.

Along with Agha, left-arm spinner Ali Usman was also recalled after being sent home from the England tour before the third and final Test.

Babar Azam will continue to lead the side in the two Tests against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi (November 9-13) and Lahore (November 17-21).

The 14-member squad includes a trio of uncapped batters – Mohammad Taha, Sameer Minhas and Mohammad Suleman – who have done well at domestic level.

The two-match series is part of the World Test Championship, with Pakistan ninth and last and Sri Lanka seventh.

articles.title: BS Meter on WWE WrestleMania 43 and Survivor Series Plans, Massive AEW Stars Return Date, More
articles.summary: The pro wrestling rumor mill has WWE WrestleMania 43 on the mind this week.
articles.body:
The pro wrestling rumor mill has WWE WrestleMania 43 on the mind this week.

That's an exclamation point of a discussion point, considering WWE's fast approaching a possible event in Saudi Arabia and AEW has a big show of its own on the way.

Naturally, the rumor mill loops in conversations about counterprogramming between the two companies, plus a major retirement and quite a few other things of note.

To help fans keep pace with the latest buzz on the rumor mill, let's put the must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss.

It feels like Toni Storm is on the way back to AEW soon. But according to Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), Storm won't actually be back competing in a ring until "2027 at the earliest."

A huge Storm marketing campaign fired up at WrestleDream in mid-October, but it didn't feel like the little hints that created viral moments were a sign of an immediate return. Fans haven't seen her in the ring since early in the year, so little hints by the month could build some serious hype, though.

We'd probably hear even more buzz if an in-ring return was about to happen. AEW seems content to dripfeed this one for the next several months, which is great: There's a lot of storyline and character stuff they could do to explain away the absence in kayfabe before a big return next year.

Let the counterprogramming talk begin in earnest. According to Wrestling Observer Live's Bryan Alvarez (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), NXT's strong showing against an episode of AEW Dynamite has given them a green light to load up big time against the upcoming Blood & Guts.

WWE hasn't had any problems counterprogramming AEW with pretty much anything in the past. But the fact a normal NXT show is sparring well in the ratings with AEW's big weekly hitters is a pretty big deal right now.

Fair enough. WWE would counterprogram Blood & Guts anyway. But feeling good about recent head-to-heads enough to take the risk makes sense. And if WWE can somehow win or come close, it's going to cause a ruckus online.

Here comes the obvious faction stuff. According to Wrestling Observer Radio's Dave Meltzer (h/t Mrosko ), WWE is indeed positioning The Bloodline to go against 946 at Survivor Series.

Cliche or not, the writing has been on the wall for a while. WWE kept Roman Reigns out of it for as long as it could, but it was stretching believability that he wouldn't take issue with, you know, his family members getting hit by cars and stuff. Now, 946 has Carmelo Hayes in the fray as another member, too, setting up the big event.

Trust that there have been much, much worse builds to a Survivor Series event. This is great. It's a great use of Hayes, and there's room for Jacob Fatu to come back for this too. Fun wrinkle: One could see Fatu actually aligning with either faction, so that's a wild card. And if he does, that probably means even more people will get involved, making the next few weeks really interesting.

A legend could be on his way out next year. According to Wrestling Observer (h/t Mrosko ), Rey Mysterio could be getting his own retirement tour next year, something called "quite possible" in the report.

It's easy to look at Mysterio's body of work and current role as a general manager and think that he wouldn't go on the long retirement tour. That feels reserved for guys like John Cena, who is just a cut above everybody else. Meaning, it's refreshing to hear Mysterio might get one.

There's way too much Mysterio could do to merely have a one-off. There's Dominik Mysterio. There's Penta. His daughter, Aalyah, is in WWE now. Others like Dragon Lee could use nods, never mind callbacks to some of his best-ever matches that are still possible, like with Randy Orton. A farewell tour is almost a must .

One predictable, one a mild surprise. Not hard to tell which is which. According to Wrestling Observer (h/t Mrosko ), WWE is still on track for Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi to main event Night 2 of WrestleMania 43. CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes, however, is not the plan for Night 1.

Call it a mild surprise. There's too much volatility around the other top championship right now to declare that Punk vs. Rhodes is inevitable. Nobody would complain if it was, but we don't know what either guy's character will look like by 'Mania, never mind what WWE wants to do with Sami Zayn, Bron Breakker and Money in the Bank briefcase holder Penta, to name a few.

Sort of an eye-rolling rumor here, really. Everything is penciled in at best around the main event scene and worked toward for months. Injuries and other changes mix things up. Reigns-Femi feels inevitable. Punk and Rhodes could just as easily not even need a title or main event in a few weeks, let alone by WrestleMania.

articles.title: New Truths About WWE and AEW Revealed in 2026
articles.summary: As 2026 comes close to an end, another important year in professional wrestling has left fans with a fresh view of both WWE and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
As 2026 comes close to an end, another important year in professional wrestling has left fans with a fresh view of both WWE and All Elite Wrestling.

From the rise of Oba Femi to the return of Roman Reigns to the top of the business, WWE offered a fresh yet also familiar look at its current direction.

While Kenny Omega and The Young Bucks seemed to begin the final chapters of their careers and Will Ospreay finally became the top guy, AEW seemed to prepare for a new Elite-less future.

This and more established new truths about the state of the two biggest wrestling companies in the world.

It did not take long for Oba Femi to make an impression in WWE, but it was 2026 that clearly showcased that he is the man WWE can build the brand around.

It has become so clear that even AEW wrestlers like Swerve Strickland are taking time out of their day to put him over.

WWE has bet everything on The Ruler, and it is already paying off. The 28-year-old star won King of the Ring despite WWE not wanting him to be world champion yet, and fans did not bat an eye.

While Gunther retired three men in one year, Oba ending the career of Brock Lesnar made The Ruler look like the true Career Killer, defeating The Beast Incarnate at both WrestleMania and SummerSlam.

While WWE repeatedly plays it slow with young stars, Oba is the exception, and fans have welcomed that change with open arms.

No one is hotter in all of WWE, and the only disappointment is that WWE keeps delaying The Ruler's true ascension, dethroning Roman Reigns.

AEW is the Only Company That Still Values Tag Team Wrestling

After letting go of both New Day and Motor City Machine Guns, WWE made a firm statement on its commitment to tag team wrestling.

The men's tag team division has been in shambles for a while as The Vision barely seem to notice their gold and The MFTs are feuding with the lowest standing stars on SmackDown.

The women's tag team division was a big part of WWE at the end of 2025 with the feud of Asuka and Kairi Sane vs. Rhea Ripley and Iyo Sky.

However, WWE released Sane while Asuka went on hiatus followed by breaking up Ripley and Sky between brands. Since that time, it has been a hot potato that has gotten no one over.

Meanwhile, AEW picked up the teams WWE let go and delivered one of its best years for tag team wrestling, led by The Young Bucks.

As FTR and MCMG continued a Best of 5 Series and the newly named New Level have delivered one of the best feuds in the history of the World Trios Championship with Hangman Adam Page and Brodido, AEW is doubling down.

The women's tag team division is still developing, but Divine Dominion raised the bar with their title reign and finished their run with the gold in two brutal, memorable battles with The Brawling Birds.

It is clear WWE has decided tag team wrestling has no value to the current product, and AEW is the only company that will deliver consistently great tag team action for years to come.

Women's Wrestlers Need to Stand Up for Themselves More

Neither WWE or AEW hold the high ground currently when it comes to women's wrestling, massively outshined by World Wonder Ring Stardom where Saya Kamitani was the biggest star in all of Japanese wrestling.

Despite repeated lip service from WWE about the importance of women's wrestling, no matches have been reportedly cut for time more often including the infamous six-minute Liv Morgan vs. Stephanie Vaquer at WrestleMania 42.

WWE Unreal highlighted Liv backstage seeking praise from Triple H for saving time in-between the two men's matches that totaled over 40 in-ring minutes.

This juxtaposes with WrestleMania 39 just three years earlier where Charlotte Flair and Rhea Ripley delivered the best match of the whole weekend going over time despite backstage annoyance.

While AEW has given more time to the women recently, especially Mercedes Moné, it still feels like the women's division is a side concern for the company where many women disappear from TV for weeks to months while healthy.

While WWE did not following up on the excellent Evolution 2025, AEW still has yet to have a women's match main event any PPV in the company's history.

It is far past time that women in wrestling stand up for themselves and advocate for their ability to be major draws like Becky Lynch, Charlotte and Ronda Rousey once did.

If the women do not advocate for their own value, this business will quickly fall back into old habits where only women-only promotions truly shine the spotlight on what women's wrestling can be.

Wrestling Thrives on Surprises More Than Long-Term Payoffs

Fans have long talked about the importance of consistency and payoffs in wrestling, but 2026 showed that fans are hungrier than the surprises.

While it is nice to live in the payoff of Cody Rhodes finally winning the big one or The Bloodline imploding after years of arguments, the path to get there delivers many flat nights.

It is important to not just be stuck in the same cycle of will-they-won't-they Judgment Day drama but also create stars and move championships in shocking ways.

When it all comes together, it is special, but WWE and AEW were at their best in 2026 when the unexpected happened, even without strong build-up.

Sami Zayn may be the best example of WWE combining long-term payoff and surprise together as he finally won the world title not once but twice.

The first win was a genuine shock at Night of Champions, making that show feel more important than it was on paper.

Though he lost it to CM Punk just nine days later, he would avenge that loss on SmackDown two months later and shockingly regain the gold.

Both were the freshest moves WWE has delivered all year, and they both paid off Zayn's long-term drive to be world champion and came almost out of nowhere to get everyone talking.

AEW delivered its own special underdog world title win as Darby Allin dethroned MJF to go on an all-time run as Men's world champion, defending the title multiple times a week.

While AEW also delivered a major payoff with Will Ospreay finally winning the Men's World Championship in Wembley Stadium, the world title scene remained fresh until that victory with multiple big title changes.

Wrestling has no off-season. It is important to keep the scene fresh and never have shows where it feels like nothing is going to happen because a pay-off is needed six months down the line.

Roman Reigns is Still WWE's Biggest Star

When Cody Rhodes dethroned Roman Reigns at WrestleMania 40, it looked like a passing of the torch moment where The American Nightmare would carry WWE forward.

Two years later, while Rhodes is still one of WWE's top guys, he is on par with multiple names including CM Punk and Randy Orton, carrying SmackDown by committee.

On Raw though, Roman Reigns has regained his throne and is clearly the biggest star. WWE has reunited The Bloodline and seemingly stated The OTC is still what matters most to the business.

The next man up to challenge Reigns for his spot will be Oba Femi, but all signs point to that story not playing out until WrestleMania 43.

Until that time, Reigns will be just about untouchable, and it is hard to imagine Rhodes will get back to the true top spot any time soon.

AEW Does Not Need MJF or Kenny Omega to Thrive

When AEW first started, the biggest star in the company was Kenny Omega. In spite of this, The Cleaner only got his second world title reign in 2026.

The next man that stepped up to be AEW's top star was MJF, who went into 2026 as a two-time world champion and added a third to his name during the year.

Both men though has suffered from multiple medical issues that have sidelined them from big shows.

Despite their absence, AEW has proved the depth of its roster by never feeling understaffed without two of the top men in the company's history.

Jon Moxley, Hangman Adam Page, Darby Allin and Will Ospreay all played key roles in driving the company forward in the past year and have fit seamlessly into a top role.

While AEW may have too many stars signed, it has led to a roster that can keep marching forward no matter what.

The only big name in AEW whose absence has been massively felt is "Timeless" Toni Storm as the women's division has yet to build as many top names to carry the weight as in the men's division.

When WWE bought Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide, many assumed the company would turn the company into NXT Mexico.

So far though, the company led by smart creative from Undertaker and Jeremy Borash has kept AAA a separate creative entity.

This has led to fresh stars like Mr. Iguana, Psycho Clown and La Parka to start selling themselves to a fresh audience.

The company has also revitalized stars like El Grande Americano and Rey Fénix. Even Omos has found a strong role on the show, helping make "Dirty" Dominik Mysterio look the star he should on Raw.

The commitment to lucha has even caused a shift in major WWE programming, especially the rise of Penta. His men's Money in the Bank win solidified that rise to stardom, promising a future world title reign is coming.

As Rey Mysterio is likely on his way to retirement, Dragon Lee has also gained a greater focus as one of multiple luchadors stepping up to fill his shoes.

WWE has never shown this much interesting in lucha libre beyond Mysterio, and it needs to continue as it adds to the variety of styles highlighted in American professional wrestling.

For better and worse, WWE only had one top man in creative for much of the company's life. When Vince McMahon was forced to retire, Paul Levesque stepped into impossibly large shoes.

The early years of Triple H at the head were promising, delivering a more focused and consistent product, creating all-time great moments in WWE.

However, that creative high has subsided, and the weekly product has grown stale.

WWE has delivered memorable moment in 2026, especially at premium live events, but outside of the Oba Femi breakout, nothing is must-see television.

Perhaps a full change at the lead position in the creative team is not needed, but WWE certainly needs fresh voices to push a stale roster into fresh positions.

It is time to figure out why most of the roster are stuck in neutral and better position younger stars to take the top spot away from the 40-year-old standard bearers.

Even if Roman Reigns, CM Punk and Cody Rhodes are still WWE's biggest names, it does not make for an interesting show to watch these same men go through the motions for months.

Whoever is going to step up, WWE needs to look at stars like Bron Breakker, "Dirty" Dominik Mysterio and Roxanne Perez to figure out what it is going to take for these stars to become the next big stars they were supposed to become years ago.

There Are Too Many Premium Live Events/Pay-Per-Views

The number of major wrestling events WWE and AEW expect fans to commit to every year is growing absolutely absurd.

WWE has 15 premium live events scheduled for the year including four Saturday Night Main Events, not to mention the still-expected John Cena Classic. Both WrestleMania and SummerSlam were also two nights this year.

NXT has 5 premium live events of its own with likely at least one more to be added in Deadline. WWE has also promoted multiple major events for Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide, especially TripleMania and Noche de Los Grandes.

Meanwhile, AEW's Pay-Per-View calendar has ballooned to 10 for the year, and it seems like the company will keep adding more in future years.

It has been difficult to find a single weekend in 2026 where the expectation was not to watch some wrestling event on top of the weekly commitments.

Even for those only watching one of the two companies, this time commitment is too high. WWE could pull back on a few main-roster events to push fans to watch more NXT to get to know the future stars.

AEW started slow with the first PPV, Revolution, not until March, but the time between PPVs has shrunk to just three weeks for the summer-to-fall PPV schedule. This has led to obvious struggles to build a full card.

Between the price of ESPN+ and monthly PPVs, WWE and AEW are expecting too much of fans and will likely lead to lower viewership due to burnout.

articles.title: Re-Ranking the Best NHL Heritage Classic Jerseys Ahead of Canadiens-Jets Game
articles.summary: While the United States gets to have the Winter Classic, Canada's NHL fans get to revel in the Heritage Classic for all the joy of outdoor hockey fans and players alike can handle.
articles.body:
While the United States gets to have the Winter Classic, Canada's NHL fans get to revel in the Heritage Classic for all the joy of outdoor hockey fans and players alike can handle.

Sunday's matchup in Winnipeg between the Winnipeg Jets and Canadiens marks the eighth Heritage Classic in league history and with it comes all of the classic Canadian joy and history we love to see from events like this and that includes special throwback style jerseys.

All seven Canadian teams as well as the honorary eighth Canadian team, the Buffalo Sabres, have played in the event and they've all brought their own kinds of style outdoors for the Heritage Classic. We're going to rank them even though many of them have become current home or road jerseys now and even though many of those are beautiful, we're giving bonus points out for doing things a little different, especially for more recent games.

On the one hand, it was awesome to see the Maple Leafs go deep into their history for the 2022 Heritage Classic in Hamilton, Ontario. Before the Leafs were born, there were the Toronto Arenas from 1917 to 1919 and this jersey was directly inspired by what that team wore way back when.

On the other hand, Leafs jerseys are outstanding and incredible and while we get what they were doing with these, they're so subdued and almost too simplistic for what's supposed to be a huge event. At least their matchup against Buffalo had some classic scraps and snowfall during the game to make it stand out.

The Canadiens matchup in Calgary in 2011's Heritage Classic was further proof that while the Habs have the perfect jerseys, it wouldn't hurt to have a few really old throwback styles in their back pocket for big events.

Montréal wore what were essentially their regular road white sweaters for the game and while those are phenomenal jerseys... it's like rolling into a Black-Tie event in regular nice clothes. Then again, since this was the second ever Heritage Classic, we could give them a pass had Calgary not gone so historically hard for their jerseys.

The 2003 Heritage Classic was the first big-time NHL game played outside and even though so much of the event had all the bells and whistles that most outdoor games have had since then, there wasn't a definitive ideal of how to do things in an old-school way.

So when the Canadiens showed up wearing their standard classic red jerseys, it made a ton of sense. It's a perfect jersey, it's hockey being played outside in obscenely cold weather, and they're matched up against the Edmonton Oilers who were able to break out their own throwbacks to help make the game look good.

It might not seem like a big deal now that the Oilers wore their 80s throwbacks for the first Heritage Classic, but at the time it was. Not only did that event feature an alumni game the day before that featured countless Hall of Fame players, but the game being in Edmonton was the right time to do a throwback jersey for a special event game.

The Oilers had last worn these white 80s style jerseys in 1997, and their current home and road set was going in a different, albeit still good but not as great, direction. Seeing these beauties back under the lights at Commonwealth Stadium in frigid conditions just hit right. It wouldn't be until 2011 that these jerseys came back full-time to stay, but on this night? It was the perfect time.

For all the walking back we did for Calgary's 2023 Heritage Classic jerseys, it's a little harder for us to do the same with Edmonton's but dang it if the color scheme doesn't crush it.

We still don't like the ribbon with the team name, but we do like the oil drop with the player number in it. But mostly we're big fans of the blue jersey with the orange and white striping and shoulders. It's got an old-fashioned feel to it and while it's definitely trying really hard to sell that point, it's unique in a mostly positive way and we're trying to be less negative these days.

Still, when you've got regular jerseys that crush it night after night the way the Oilers do, going away from that almost always means there's a downgrade.

At the time the jerseys were released for the 2023 Heritage Classic, we were pretty harsh on them because, boy, they were trying pretty hard to be old school for both the Flames and Oilers. Time heals most wounds though and we can feel a little bit better about Calgary's sweaters now.

The circular style logo was overdone years ago and encasing the Flames' logo like that goes against the nature of beauty, but with the way the rest of the jersey is designed, we get it better now. The vintage white with the red shoulders and stripes on the sleeves are fine.

Instead of being outright haters of this, we've settled down and think these are perfectly cromulent jerseys instead.

The Sabres became the first U.S. team to play in the Heritage Classic in 2022 and to celebrate that, they didn't really mess with a good thing at all apart from one obvious distinction.

The Sabres kept their perfect logo along with blue, gold and white stripes and instead of a regular white jersey, they used a vintage, cream white instead. They also ditched the blue and gold shoulder yoke for the game because that's a bit too modern for a throwback-style look. It's a great, clean looking jersey and for an event that was meant for the Leafs to stomp on their American neighbors, the Sabres won 5-2 in Hamilton instead and provided this very meme-y photo of now former Sabres forward Dylan Cozens.

The Canadiens history of jerseys doesn't exactly allow for a lot of different looks and frankly, that's totally fine because why mess with perfection, right?

What the Habs are doing for the Heritage Classic this season is interesting because it calls back to the 1920s and 1930s but also serves as a nod to 1991-1992 when they broke out this particular jersey in celebration of the NHL's 75th anniversary that season.

The classic logo on the red sweater with blue and white stripes is as iconic as it gets, but the blue stripe on the left sleeve also gets a small version of the Canadiens logo embedded in it as well. The number and name fonts are modernized which gives it a new twist of sorts, but it's still as classic of a look as you get with the Canadiens.

These dark blue beauties from the Winnipeg Jets days before joining the NHL were a great choice for the team in the 2019 Heritage Classic matchup against Calgary. The Jets logo from back in the day is a real product of the era given how similar in style it is to the Edmonton Oilers and New York Islanders in ways and throwing it on the front of a jersey is a great way to make it memorable.

The Jets liked wearing these for the Heritage Classic so much they made it their alternate jersey in 2021 and every time we see them, we want to see more jerseys like them because we're suckers for nostalgia in the best way.

No, we're not cheating here by doubling up teams, it's just that the Winnipeg Jets jerseys they're wearing for this year's Heritage Classic are the same that they wore for the 2016 Heritage Classic as well. Look!

It's somewhat fitting the Jets are doing this because they're hosting the event this season and have spent the past couple of days bringing back Jets players from their recent past including Dustin Byfuglien, Blake Wheeler and more. There was also an alumni game against Canadiens alums on Saturday night.

But these jerseys? They're great and also the white version of the dark blue alternates the team wears during the season that they also wore during the 2019 Heritage Classic.

For the 2019 Heritage Classic, the Flames made everything old new again by breaking out their former home white sweaters from the 80s and 90s. They were already wearing their red ones as an alternate at home by this point, but the white ones were left in the past...until this game.

As great as their red sweaters are, the white jerseys pop just as hard. The logo stands out brighter and the stripes and shoulder are so, so good. Bringing back these classics in 2019 got fans excited to see them more often and the team did that in 2021 on a full-time basis and continues to wear them now. They're also one of our most favorite road sweaters in the league.

When the Senators and Canucks squared off in 2014's Heritage Classic, it gave Ottawa the opportunity to flip their current alternate jersey, a vintage style black jersey with a large "O" as the crest and make it vintage white.

The Sens alternate of this time frame was excellent and the nods it provided to the original Ottawa Senators of the early 1900s were great. From the black and red stripes and simple logo, it was an ideal alternate look. That they took it and made it a white road jersey for the Heritage Classic might sound lazy, but when you saw it in full display, it was anything but that.

The one big downer with these jerseys is that we saw them for this event and almost never again. Too bad.

If you memory holed something about the Oilers from the first few seasons of Connor McDavid taking over the NHL, forgetting that they wore these orange alternate jerseys for two seasons and then made them their home jerseys for five more years after that would almost be understandable.

Seeing them now after not seeing them for multiple years makes us remember how nice they were as an alternate jersey. After all, these jerseys were like what the team wore for the first two years of its existence in the WHA and when they made it their jersey for the 2016 Heritage Classic... it was already their alternate jersey and had been around for a season. Sigh.

Looking back without that information, this jersey was an incredible choice to wear for the game. But having those facts really makes it seem like such a letdown. Still, a great looking jersey deserves credit, and this is definitely one.

The 2014 Heritage Classic might be more memorable for being played indoors at BC Place or for then Canucks coach John Tortorella starting Cory Schneider instead of Roberto Luongo, but it should be best remembered for Vancouver breaking out the striped "V" of the Vancouver Millionaires.

The Millionaires existed from 1911 to 1926 and the uniforms the Canucks wore for the Heritage Classic were directly designed from those teams. The Millionaires were Stanley Cup champions in 1915 and if you're going to host a big-time event in Vancouver, paying homage to the original champions of the city was a great way to do it.

The maroon and cream striped sleeves and the giant "V" crest with "Vancouver" spelled out in it were incredible to see. If there's a downside it's that the jerseys weren't actually wool, but we're going to give that a pass for a few reasons. Whenever the Canucks get back to a Heritage Classic (or maybe a Winter Classic...) they've got plenty from their own history to bring back to life, but for the first one, we're more than happy they went way back into history.

The Flames logo is perfect. The Flames colors of red and gold are also perfect for hockey, especially when your team's name has to do with fire. Given the Flames' limited history of throwback jerseys in 2011 and needing to have something old-timey for hosting the Heritage Classic, they threw it back to a really old-fashioned style of jersey and went wild with the stripes.

Stripes on the jersey and even more stripes up and down the sleeves all in red and gold. They're glorious and incredible and every team has been playing for second in trying to make it look good outdoors when trying to look like a team from a century ago.

articles.title: Is Puka Nacua playing today? Latest on Rams WR's Week 7 status
articles.summary: Puka Nacua is questionable to play against the Raiders today. Here's the latest on the Rams' star receiver.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua injured his calf in practice on Thursday, causing panic to set in among fans. He then sat out Friday's practice and was given a questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders .

It's not the way the Rams hoped to enter this pivotal game, especially given all the injuries they've suffered over the last few weeks. Puka Nacua is arguably their most important player besides Matthew Stafford, so losing him for any amount of time is costly.

What is Nacua's status for today's game? Here's the latest on what we know about the Rams' star receiver.

Sean McVay said on Friday that Nacua is questionable and will work out before the game in an attempt to determine his status. It's not a good sign that he was unable to practice on Friday, but he wasn't ruled out or given a doubtful tag, so there's at least a chance he'll suit up.

The Rams are already without Davante Adams after he ruptured his hamstring last week against the Cardinals , so their wide receiver depth chart is getting thin.

articles.title: Vote! Who should be Register-Guard girls Athlete of the Week?
articles.summary: This week's nominees are from Creswell, Marist Catholic, North Eugene, Pleasant Hill, Sheldon, South Eugene, Triangle Lake and Willamette.
articles.body:
The fall prep sports postseason is just around the corner, and athletes throughout the Eugene-Springfield area have continued to produce stellar performances.

Every week, you get to vote for The Register-Guard's Athlete of the Week.

Here are the nominees for this week's boys Athlete of the Week based on performances from Oct. 17-23.

Austyn Hartwig, Triangle Lake cross-country

Nellie Smith, Pleasant Hill cross-country

Information about each nominee is listed below. Vote for the athlete you think is most deserving at registerguard.com/sports. The poll closes at 9 a.m. Thursday.

South Eugene senior Lucy Alkire racked up 35 assists and 12 digs Oct. 20 to lead the Class 6A No. 9 Axe to a 3-1 win over Class 5A No. 10 Churchill.

Sheldon senior setter Addison Brandow recorded 55 assists over the course of two matches last week, helping the Irish to road wins over Willamette and Springfield.

Willamette sophomore defensive midfielder Rose Chunn delivered strong showings in the Wolverines' Oct. 20 0-0 draw against Sheldon and Oct. 22 3-1 win at Churchill.

"She was great in stopping the ball in the middle as well as starting our attack," Willamette coach Christine Guldager said. "She plays with heart and passion each game."

South Eugene senior Sofia Collins tallied 11 kills and eight digs Oct. 20 to lead the Class 6A No. 9 Axe to a 3-1 win over Class 5A No. 10 Churchill.

Creswell senior midfielder Kendall Durflinger scored the winning goal on a header Oct. 21 to lift the Class 3A/2A/1A No. 8 Bulldogs to a 1-0 home win over No. 14 Central Linn.

That goal secured the Mountain Valley Conference title for Creswell.

Triangle Lake sophomore Austyn Hartwig ran a 5,000-meter personal best time of 20 minutes, 28.5 seconds Oct. 21 and finished 12th at the Umpqua Invite.

Hartwig's time is the 14th-fastest in the state this season among Class 2A/1A girls.

Marist Catholic junior defender Lexi Hudson scored a goal Oct. 20 in the Spartans' 9-0 home win over Cottage Grove, and another Oct. 22 in their 8-0 win at North Bend.

"Lexi, who now has seven goals and two assists this season, is our team's fourth-leading scorer as our starting center back," Marist Catholic coach Stefan Schroffner said. "Lexi is the captain of our defensive backline and has been critical in helping Marist's defense notch 12 shutouts in 14 games."

Marist Catholic sophomore midfielder Alyssa McManus delivered an assist Oct. 20 in the Spartans' 9-0 home win over Cottage Grove and also had an assist Oct. 22 in their 8-0 win at North Bend.

"Alyssa has five goals and seven assists, but what makes her valuable is that she is a true box-to-box, sideline-to-sideline midfielder," Marist Catholic coach Stefan Schroffner said. "She is technical with great vision and will simply outwork anyone she plays against. She does all the dirty work for us; helps in defense and attack."

Willamette freshman midfielder Brinly Morrison scored a brace Oct. 22 in the Wolverines' 3-1 road win over Churchill.

Sheldon senior libero Natalie Shoemaker racked up a career-high seven aces Oct. 22 in the Irish's win at Springfield.

Pleasant Hill junior Nellie Smith ran a personal-best 5,000 time of 19:59.1 Oct. 21 to finish eighth at the Umpqua Invite.

Smith's time is the 19th-fastest in the state this season among Class 3A girls.

North Eugene sophomore goalkeeper Madison Stuart played a big role in the Class 5A No. 1 Highlanders' 2-1 win over No. 12 Thurston on Oct. 22.

"Madison was outstanding. Made a couple of big saves, including a one-on-one save," North Eugene coach Jamie Tait said.

North Eugene junior center back Luci Tait helped the Class 5A No. 1 Highlanders secure a close-fought 2-1 win over No. 12 Thurston on Oct. 22.

"She was solid in our backline; won balls out of the air and kept (Thurston's) forwards under pressure," North Eugene coach Jamie Tait said.

To submit an Athlete of the Week nomination, please email Register-Guard sports reporter Jarrid Denney at jdenney@registerguard.com with the athlete's name, stats and any other relevant information about the performance they are being nominated for.

articles.title: The top 25 modern golf courses in Canada, ranked
articles.summary: Our ranking of top modern Canadian courses returns, with Nos. 1 and 2 sitting side by side.
articles.body:
Welcome to the Golfweek's Best 2026 ranking of the top 25 modern golf courses in Canada. Golfweek for many years ranked Canadian courses, but during COVID there wasn't much movement on the lists of best modern and classic courses in the country, so the rankings were paused. Now we're bringing them back.

The hundreds of members of our course-ratings panel continually evaluate courses around the world, and their individual ratings on a 10-point basis are averaged to produce these rankings. The top handful of courses in the world have an average rating of above 9, while many excellent layouts fall into the high-6 to the 8 range. Click here to learn more about how we rate courses.

This ranking list focuses only on modern courses, with 1960 as a break point between modern and classic courses. Why 1960? As noted in our rater's handbook that guides these rankings, design and construction techniques for courses shifted fundamentally after 1960. Mechanized earth-moving became the norm. Most courses required extensive planning, documentation and meticulous excavation. While the advent of new, high-performance grasses meant better conditions, the quicker putting speeds meant greens could not be built with the same dramatic slopes as with many classic courses built before 1960. The skills required to build a great course became those of professionally trained landscape architects, not just creative golf visionaries. The industry had changed dramatically.

articles.title: Tres parejas, un trono: la batalla por el número uno femenino entra en su fase decisiva
articles.standfirst: Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea defienden el liderato frente al impulso de Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero y las aspiraciones de Bea González y Paula Josemaría, con 6.500 puntos todavía en juego
articles.summary: Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea defienden el liderato frente al impulso de Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero y las aspiraciones de Bea González y Paula Josemaría, con 6.500 puntos todavía en juego
articles.body: La temporada femenina de Premier Padel se acerca a su desenlace con una incógnita que mantiene en vilo a las principales protagonistas del circuito: quién cerrará el año en lo más alto de la Race. Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea conservan el mando, pero la distancia con sus perseguidoras se ha estrechado y el calendario todavía ofrece margen para un cambio de escenario. Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero han irrumpido con fuerza en la discusión, mientras Bea González y Paula Josemaría continúan al acecho. Tres parejas, tres caminos distintos y un objetivo que convierte cada partido en una pieza importante de la lucha por el trono. Gemma y Delfi tienen a su favor el trabajo acumulado durante toda la temporada. Su regularidad les ha permitido alcanzar la recta final desde la primera posición, aunque sus últimas actuaciones han dejado abierta una puerta que sus rivales quieren aprovechar. La pareja hispano argentina sabe que no necesita ganar todos los torneos para conservar el liderato, pero sí evitar que sus perseguidoras encadenen nuevos resultados importantes. Con 12.020 puntos, mantienen una ventaja considerable; aun así, el número uno todavía exige una última demostración de autoridad. Quienes más han cambiado el paisaje de esta carrera son Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero. Su rendimiento reciente ha convertido una temporada de adaptación y crecimiento en una candidatura real a la cima: han disputado tres finales consecutivas durante la gira europea y levantado los títulos de Rotterdam y Milán, además del Major de París en las últimas cuatro citas. La victoria en Italia, donde superaron a Gemma y Delfi en semifinales antes de derrotar a Bea y Paula en la final, confirmó que están preparadas para competir de tú a tú con cualquiera. Con 10.040 puntos, se sitúan a 1.980 de las líderes. Una diferencia que invita a soñar, especialmente cuando todavía quedan 6.500 puntos por repartir. El Kuwait Major aparece como la primera gran prueba para comprobar hasta dónde puede llegar esa amenaza. Un buen resultado de Ari y Andrea podría comprimir todavía más la clasificación y trasladar la presión a las actuales número uno. Si las catalanas conquistan el título y Triay-Brea no alcanzan la final, la distancia podría reducirse hasta los 700 puntos. No se trata únicamente de sumar: también importa cuánto dejan de sumar las rivales. En una carrera tan ajustada, una derrota inesperada puede tener tanto peso como levantar un trofeo. Y con el Dubai P1 y el Major de México todavía por delante, cualquier movimiento en Kuwait puede alterar el rumbo de las últimas semanas. Bea González y Paula Josemaría afrontan una misión más exigente, pero no están fuera de la conversación. Ambas comparten con Triay y Brea el registro de seis títulos esta temporada, una cifra que refleja la capacidad de la pareja para dominar el circuito. Para aspirar al número uno necesitan recuperar terreno cuanto antes y dependerán también de los resultados de las dos parejas que tienen por delante. Su potencial competitivo no está en cuestión; el desafío es transformar ese nivel en una combinación de resultados que las devuelva a la pelea por el liderato. La recta final no ofrece garantías para nadie. Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea parten con ventaja y la experiencia de quienes han sabido sostenerse arriba; Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero llegan con confianza, títulos recientes y la sensación de estar creciendo en el momento perfecto; Bea González y Paula Josemaría necesitan una reacción que vuelva a colocarlas en el centro de la batalla. Kuwait puede no decidirlo todo, pero sí marcar quién llega al último tramo con opciones reales y quién se ve obligado a depender de terceros. El número uno sigue en manos de las actuales líderes, aunque ya no basta con mirar la clasificación para dar por resuelta la temporada.

articles.title: Jordan's Review: Auburn defense was a letdown in loss to LSU
articles.summary: Phillip Jordan sheds light on Auburn's defensive struggles in its 38-17 loss to LSU on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Auburn Tigers could not continue last week's momentum as they lost their third game of the season with a 38-17 defeat to No. 18 LSU .

In the upset victory over Georgia last week, Auburn was able to control the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball. In defeat to LSU, Auburn lost the battle in week eight. LSU made a point to slow down the rushing of Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown and put plenty of pressure on the signal caller. Brown gained just 21 yards on 19 carries and was sacked seven times. He did have a big run of 34 yards to the one-yard line with Auburn down 17-3 in the second quarter. Brown capped off that drive with a score of one-yard to make the game 17-10 in the favor of LSU with 9:48 in the second quarter.

The LSU offense took the game over after that score for 21 unanswered points, and carried a 31-10 lead into halftime. The Auburn defense was the biggest letdown on Saturday. In the first half alone, Auburn gave up 346 yards and 18 first downs on 44 plays. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt looked like an All-American in the game. In the first half, he was 21-of-27 for 261 yards and three touchdowns. Leavitt finished the game with 387 passing yards and 54 yards on the ground with a rushing touchdown. LSU's total yards in the game were 552.

That is not the standard of this team or the defense.

"Definitely not the standard to our defense. We just have to come out, play faster, and start fast," linebacker Elijah Melendez said postgame.

The Auburn run defense did not have much luck either in the loss. LSU rushed for 165 yards and averaged 4.9 yards per carry. Dilin Jones led the way for LSU with 92 yards and one touchdown. On the Auburn side, they only rushed for 67 yards in the game. Running backs Jeremiah Cobb and Omar Mabson combined for just 27 yards. "We just weren't good enough, and we didn't find enough creative ways to create the run game," said Alex Golesh after the game.

A big part of LSU's scoring drives in the first half was the Auburn defense's inability to get off the field on key third and fourth downs. LSU was 5-of-13 on third down, but they were also 3-of-4 on fourth down. When the Auburn defense has struggled this season, getting off the field in key situations has been a major contributor.

Things will not get easier for the defense next week when they face one of the best quarterbacks in the country, Ole Miss signal caller Trinidad Chambliss.

articles.title: College football rankings after Week 8: Updated Coaches Poll, AP Top 25 for SEC
articles.summary: Here's where SEC teams were ranked in the latest US LBM Coaches Poll and AP Top 25 after Week 8:
articles.body:
The SEC was home to one of the most entertaining games of the Week 8 college football schedule — and one of its biggest upsets.

The latter of those came in Columbia, South Carolina, where an unranked Gamecocks team upended No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 . LaNorris Sellers completed 18 of 32 passes for 210 yards and a score, adding a game-tying rushing touchdown in the game's final minutes — with a Herculean effort — to help lead the Gamecocks to the upset.

Dylan Stewart, who was suspended earlier this season, provided the defensive play of the game when he knocked the ball loose from George MacIntyre's hands to set up a walk-off field goal for Shane Beamer's squad.

Elsewhere, Arch Manning and No. 18 Texas nearly suffered a third-straight second-half collapse at home vs. No. 7 Ole Miss , but held on long enough to eke out a 34-27 win . Manning completed 18 of 30 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown to two interceptions while getting strip-sacked, but still rushed for two touchdowns to help Texas get back in the win column.

Credit to Ole Miss, which not only scored 21 straight points to tie the game 24-24 in the second half, but also executed a near-perfect late-game sequence in which it kicked a field goal, recovered an onside kick and made it inside the Texas 30-yard line before Trinidad Chambliss' last-second heave to the end zone was intercepted as time expired.

In Tuscaloosa, a 13th-ranked Alabama team decimated by injuries also avoided a third straight loss against Texas A&M. The Crimson Tide seemed on the verge of another second-half snoozer against Mike Elko's Aggies, but scored its first second-half touchdowns since Week 5 to beat Texas A&M 31-20. The Crimson Tide is now on bye, and it could not have come at a better time.

What channel is Dolphins vs. Jets on today?

articles.title: Takeaways from Colorado's disastrous 57-24 loss to Oklahoma State
articles.summary: Oklahoma State fell to Colorado after an abysmal second-half collapse. Here are five takeaways from the Buffaloes' fifth straight loss.
articles.body:
What started as a close halftime game with the Colorado Buffaloes on top turned into a massacre against the Oklahoma State Cowboys , who won 57-24 after scoring 37 unanswered points, including 34 in the second half.

With the talent Oklahoma State has on offense, including quarterback Drew Mestemaker who is considered a potential Heisman candidate, it is no surprise this game came down to who had the more explosive offense. The surprise is how different Colorado looked in the second half than in the first.

After such an embarrassing loss, questions remain about this program's future, including who should stay on the coaching staff after this year and who their quarterback should be.

Here is everything we learned from Colorado's degrading loss to Oklahoma State.

Colorado cannot play four complete quarters

Going into halftime, Colorado led 24-23. They went toe-to-toe with Oklahoma State offensively, and it looked like an offensive shootout. But the Buffaloes' offense did nothing after halftime, while the Cowboys' offense looked even better in the second half. This was eerily similar to how Colorado played against Utah, just flipped. In the first half against the Utes, the Buffs did nothing, but they made it a highly competitive game in the second half. Clearly, Colorado can't play football for a full 60 minutes. They seem to top out around the 30-minute mark. They won't win another game if they keep this inconsistent play up for the rest of the season.

It may be time to move on from Deion Sanders

After starting the season 2-0 with a thrilling win against Georgia Tech and Weber State, the Buffaloes have lost their last five games. They are playing uninspired football, with drastic shifts during games and they can't get consistent play out of their offense. After an embarrassing loss like this, with a halftime lead, the program needs to change. With the Buffaloes having won only five games since the start of the 2025 season, the problem seems to lie with the head coach. Nothing is likely to happen during the season, but we may be seeing the last of Sanders in Boulder.

Isaac Wilson should finish the season at quarterback

Statistically, Isaac Wilson didn't have a bad game. Most of his counting stats came in the first half, but he finished the game completing 70.4% of his passes, throwing for 280 yards and two touchdowns. He threw two interceptions in the third quarter, which hurt, but the Buffaloes were already going downhill after his costly fumble early in the second half. Given the quarterbacks Colorado has available, they should stick with Wilson for the rest of the season, but will need to completely reevaluate the position in the offseason.

The Buffaloes cannot run the ball consistently

Colorado started the season with three straight games with at least 180 rushing yards. Then, they had two straight games with under 100 rushing yards, but rebounded with 138 rushing yards against Utah. The team's running game struggled significantly against Oklahoma State, totaling just 56 rushing yards. That was their lowest output since they managed only 51 rushing yards against West Virginia last season. The Go-Go offense was meant to emphasize the run game, but over seven games, it hasn't elevated that aspect of the offense.

The Buffaloes have a turnover problem on both sides of the ball. Offensively, they now have 16 turnovers, including three against Oklahoma State. It is their third game of the season with at least three turnovers, after turning it over four times against Northwestern and Texas Tech. On the other side of the ball, Colorado's defense cannot force turnovers. This is their second game without generating a turnover, and they have only seven takeaways through seven games. After this season, they need to look in the transfer portal for players who can make a play on the ball and change the course of a game.

articles.summary: Tras hacerse con la modalidad clásica, en apenas 48 horas se lleva también el título en esta disciplina que debutada a nivel continental
articles.body: Sólo 48 horas después de proclamarse campeón de Europa de ajedrez en la modalidad clásica, Daniel Eduardo Pulvett volvió a lo más alto del podio en Creta (Grecia), esta vez gracias al oro en partidas rápidas de ajedrez para ciegos, una disciplina que debutada en este torneo. Se trata de una modalidad donde una partida dura entre 20 y 50 minutos en total. Pulvett, que representaba a la Federación Española de Deportes para Ciegos (FEDC), llegó empatado al final de las nueve rondas con el gran maestro polaco Tazbir, que en la actualidad es el campeón del mundo de esta modalidad y acudió a Grecia únicamente a disputar esta disciplina. El sistema de desempate favoreció a Pulvett que, en menos de 48 horas y tras nueve partidas, se alzó con su segundo título consecutivo, demostrando ser el rey de Europa del ajedrez para ciegos en la actualidad. “Regreso a España muy contento y feliz de conseguir estos dos trofeos por los que tanto he trabajado”, señaló antes de coger el vuelo de vuelta a Madrid. Como reconoce el técnico de la FEDC, Pablo Martínez, “para Daniel está competición con este ritmo de juego tiene mayor dificultad, porque él juega de cabeza. Son posiciones muy complejas, con poco tiempo y donde tiene que tomar decisiones rápidas para lo cual debe estar muy concentrado y no desubicar ninguna de esas piezas de su cabeza”. Para Martínez “la actuación del equipo español ha sido sobresaliente” porque los tres ajedrecistas que han disputado el torneo “han mejorado sus puntuaciones ELO en ambas modalidades”. Para este éxito “ha sido muy importante la cohesión que ha habido entre todos nosotros y el tiempo que hemos dedicado cada día de competición”, concluyó.

articles.title: Joel Embiid urges fans to ‘put pressure’ on Philadelphia 76ers to let him play back-to-back games
articles.summary: Joel Embiid’s health has been a cause for concern for the Philadelphia 76ers for years, but the superstar is ready to take on some more responsibility this s...
articles.body:
Joel Embiid's health has been a cause for concern for the Philadelphia 76ers for years, but the superstar is ready to take on some more responsibility this season.

Embiid and the 76ers continued their winning ways with a victory against the Milwaukee Bucks, thus moving them to 3-0 this season.

But now, the 76ers will have little time to revel in the spoils of victory, as they play the Detroit Pistons tonight in their first back-to-back this season.

Joel Embiid wants Philadelphia 76ers coaching staff to let him play back-to-back games

Speaking to reporters after the Philadelphia 76ers beat the Milwaukee Bucks, Joel Embiid was asked whether he would be playing in the second game of their back-to-back slate against the Detroit Pistons.

In typical Embiid fashion, the former MVP joked that he needed everyone to put pressure on the 76ers coaching staff to give him the all-clear and let him play, pointing to the fact that he had a few days to rest before last night's win.

Embiid said: "I have no idea. I actually want to play tomorrow, so can you guys put pressure on them? I don't know. You don't have to ask them, but obviously, you got three days off. Could have been two, but you get three days off.

"But it doesn't really matter. It's all about the season going well. So I guess the more time you can get to recover, the better, and then get used to it. But yeah, I want to play tomorrow. So I'll start writing articles."

So far this season, Embiid hasn't just looked healthy, but has also been playing at the high level fans became accustomed to during his MVP years.

Embiid put up a triple-double, scoring 28 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists, along with a steal, thus delivering his best outing this season.

Across his first three games, Embiid has averaged 21.7 points, 9.7 rebounds, 5.7 assists, 1.0 steal, and 1.0 block per game.

Unfortunately, Embiid's efficiency has been less than stellar, shooting just 39.2% from the field, 21.4% from deep, and 81.5% from the charity stripe.

articles.title: Colts legend questions Sauce Gardner trade
articles.summary: Colts legend Dwight Freeney explains why Sauce Gardner's fit in Indianapolis' defense raises questions about the blockbuster trade.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts' blockbuster trade for Sauce Gardner has drawn a measured question from one of the franchise's greatest pass rushers.

Pro Football Hall of Famer Dwight Freeney said Gardner is an outstanding cornerback, but wondered whether his skill set matches the way Indianapolis plays defense.

"I don't know if he was the right fit for our team," Freeney said during Friday's 'Up & Adams' appearance.

Freeney explained that the Colts use considerable zone coverage under defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo, mixing in man-to-man assignments instead of asking their top cornerback to shadow a receiver on every snap.

Considering Indianapolis surrendered two first-round picks to acquire Gardner from the New York Jets in November 2025, Freeney suggested those resources might have been better directed toward an impact pass rusher.

His reasoning was based on quicker pressure forcing quarterbacks to release the ball sooner, making coverage easier for everyone behind the line of scrimmage.

His remarks were a critique of roster construction and schematic fit, without pointing to a decline of Gardner that some believe.

Gardner will miss Sunday's matchup against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings because of a calf injury, leaving the Colts without their top cornerback against Justin Jefferson.

articles.title: Auston Matthews explains why Maple Leafs’ locker room is ‘so much fun’ right now
articles.summary: Toronto’s supportive locker room is helping everyone contribute to the team’s success.
articles.body:
The Toronto Maple Leafs are enjoying a strong run of results, and captain Auston Matthews thinks the atmosphere inside the locker room is helping drive their success in early 2026-27 NHL season. Toronto has won four consecutive games, including Saturday's impressive 7-2 victory over the Edmonton Oilers .

Matthews said the team's competitive spirit and strong relationships have created an enjoyable environment. Players are pushing each other while keeping things relaxed away from the ice.

"The locker room, day in and day out, it's been great. The environment is just so much fun," Matthews said. "It's competitive. Guys are – a lot of joking around and a lot of chirping at each other. It's just a lot of fun.

"I think that emotion and that energy carries over to the game."

The captain also emphasized that the team's collective mindset matters more than individual achievements.

"It doesn't matter who scores, everybody is excited," Matthews said. "Everything is about the team, and that's what's most important and what's driving us right now."

That approach has produced encouraging results for Toronto. After an inconsistent start to the 2026-27 season, the Maple Leafs have found their rhythm with balanced scoring and improved performances across the lineup.

Maple Leafs' young players add energy to Toronto's locker room

Goaltender Anthony Stolarz has also noticed the positive atmosphere surrounding the team. He credited the younger players with bringing fresh energy into the locker room.

" The vibes are great . We've got a great group, and the influx of kids brings a lot of energy," Stolarz said. "They're bringing out the best in everyone."

Stolarz added that the group is developing strong chemistry as the season progresses. His comments support Matthews' belief that the team's culture is becoming an important part of its success.

"It's an exciting time to be a Maple Leaf, and the team is gelling really well," Stolarz said.

Toronto's latest victory showcased that collective approach. William Nylander scored twice to reach 300 career NHL goals, while Matthews, Jack Roslovic, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri also scored.

Stolarz stopped 30 shots as the Maple Leafs overwhelmed Edmonton. Leon Draisaitl scored twice for the Oilers, but Toronto's depth proved decisive.

The Maple Leafs improved to 7-4-2 with their fourth straight win. Maintaining that chemistry will be crucial as they look to build on their recent momentum and establish greater consistency throughout the season.

articles.title: Watch: MS Dhoni has a message for younger generations like GenZ and Gen Alpha
articles.summary: MS Dhoni has urged Gen Z and Gen Alpha to stay physically active, play sports and make healthier food choices. Speaking alongside Javed Akhtar, Dhoni warned...
articles.body:
Former India captain MS Dhoni has shared an important message for Gen Z and Gen Alpha, urging young people to stay physically active and take better care of their health. Speaking at an event alongside renowned writer Javed Akhtar, Dhoni focused on how modern lifestyles, long hours of sitting and unhealthy eating habits can affect young people in the long run. The discussion began with a question about what advice they would give to younger generations, who are dealing with difficult situations and emotional challenges. While Akhtar praised the younger generation, Dhoni chose to highlight their physical well-being. Javed Akhtar said today's young people are better than previous generations in several ways. He admitted that his generation was often caught up in its own beliefs and principles, while young people today are showing stronger moral values. Akhtar suggested that older generations should learn from the youth instead of assuming they always have the answers. Dhoni, however, said he still had some advice to offer, particularly when it came to health and everyday habits.

Dhoni urges Gen Z to play sports and stay active

Dhoni explained that earlier generations naturally moved around more, which helped them digest food and maintain a healthier lifestyle. Today, people can travel from home to work using services, spend most of the day sitting in an office and then return home by car. He warned that this lack of physical activity, combined with the growing popularity of fast food, could lead to health problems later in life. Dhoni also pointed out that sugary and fried foods can be especially harmful when people do not get enough exercise.

His advice to young people was simple: make physical activity and sports part of their daily routine. Even if an inactive lifestyle does not cause immediate problems, its effects may become more noticeable after the age of 30. The former India captain's message was a reminder that staying healthy requires consistent effort. Along with managing modern-day pressures, young people should prioritise exercise, make healthier food choices and develop habits that support their long-term well-being.

articles.summary: Ex-world champion Joe Cordina says the opportunity to fight boxing legend Manny Pacquiao on the Anthony Joshua v Tyson Fury card would "be an honour".
articles.body:
Former IBF super-featherweight champion Joe Cordina says the opportunity to fight Manny Pacquiao would "be an honour".

The proposed bout, for which negotiations are at an advanced stage, would be on the undercard of the Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury fight in Cordina's home city of Cardiff on 11 December.

The 34-year-old, who was recently cleared of assault charges, hopes a fight against one of boxing's all-time greats would help "skyrocket" his career.

"In 100 years' time, world titles will still be there - a legend like Manny Pacquiao will never come again," Cordina told BBC Sport Wales.

"For me to share the ring with him would be unbelievable for me, he's someone I grew up watching before I was even boxing."

Pacquiao, 47, has not fought since July 2025, having returned from his second attempt at retirement.

The Filipino icon is a 12-time world champion across eight different weights.

"He's done everything in the sport," added Cordina.

"He's getting on, but he still showed that he can compete with the best.

"If it happens it's unbelievable for me and it's a dream come true, I've always wanted those big fights and big names."

The Welshman however insists he would not be overawed if the fight goes ahead.

"I've not got it twisted. I'm not going to go in there and be shy, be starstruck by Manny Pacquia," the two-time world champion said.

"But this potentially could change my whole life and skyrocket me to the moon. It's a massive opportunity."

Cordina's promoter Eddie Hearn admits it is still uncertain whether the final details can be agreed, but said the Welsh fighter "must feature" on what will be one of the highly anticipated boxing cards in recent years.

"We have agreed terms, we got made an offer which we accepted, but I'm hearing today (Saturday) that it's a bit unsure whether Manny Pacquiao will feature on that card," said Hearn.

"But for me Joe Cordina must feature on that card. I think he's the most successful fighter from Wales in many years, he's a two-time world champion and he lives round the corner.

"So if it's not Manny Pacquiao what about Abdullah Mason? What about even a Shakur Stevenson or Keyshawn Davis?

"Joe is ready to fight any of these guys on 11 December and we're pushing hard to make that happen."

Earlier this week, Cordina was cleared of assault charges following an incident outside a petrol station in Pentwyn, Cardiff, in February.

The former Olympian was set to fight American Mason for the WBO lightweight title in Cleveland in July, but was denied a visa after being charged.

"It took a toll on me, my family and obviously financially it hit me quite hard because I lost out on a fight through it," said Cordina.

"I knew when it got down to the nitty-gritty that the evidence that was there and I knew that outcome would be the case.

"I was assaulted - all I did was defend myself."

Cordina insists the incident will not change how he interacts with members of the public.

"I get noticed maybe five or six times a day, sometimes people call me over, people want photos," Cordina added.

"I'm in the public eye and I believe part and parcel of what I do is being involved with people, interacting with people and interacting with the public.

"Some people might be having a bad day and just that little chat might make their day so, I wouldn't do anything different."

articles.title: Injury update: Will Sauce Gardner face the Vikings in Week 7?
articles.summary: Will the Vikings have to worry about Sauce Gardner in Week 7?
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are back from their Bye Week and ready to take on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7.

Both teams are dealing with a handful of injuries that could swing the matchup in one team's favor or the other. In this piece, we are discussing the status of Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner. The All-Pro cornerback has been dealing with a calf strain, and his status for Week 7 and beyond has been in question.

Gardner has been ruled out for Week 7 and could miss even longer. The team is likely to take things slowly with their top cornerback and defender in a season that is quickly slipping away from them. Since being acquired last season from the New York Jets, the Colts have not had the return they had hoped for.

That may be part of the reason that their general manager, Chris Ballard, was fired this week.
